Pattern of control_zoom_on / control_zoom_off.json. Original label of control.json: v4 control (hri_control_v4.py): POINT / WAIT / STOP dialog, roadmap resolution of the pointed direction, zoom rule. docs/project_flow_v4.md, docs/gesture_reader_v4.md.
declared: 2026-10-24, before any v4 recording exists. Values marked initial are TO BE SET ON DEVELOPMENT DATA; none is tuned. Drive, safety and the other dialog timings come from the frozen v3 file below (read only, unchanged).
roadmap_note: P7 (2026-11-12, Nusrat during Anisha's absence; AUDIT.md section 15): the v4 map, with the start node A asking first (P8). The v3 map configs/roadmap.json is unchanged and no longer read by v4.

why.gesture_hold_s: Overrides the v3 value (1.0 s). INITIAL. The reader already requires the arm to be still for hold_min_s (0.4 s) and the pose to pass its cues in 70 per cent of the frames; the dialog adds 0.5 s of the same resolved branch (5 frames at 10 Hz), the MOVE hold of the v3 decision rules. To be set on development data.
why.branch_match_max_deg: INITIAL. Largest angle between a pointed direction (world yaw) and the nearest valid branch for the robot to take it. The branches of the roadmap are 90 deg apart; 30 deg leaves a 30 deg band between two branches in which the answer is unclear (ask again), like the v3 reader's 15 deg tolerance around 45 deg spaced directions. The reader's foreshortening makes the angle uncertain by tens of degrees for out-of-plane arms, so a smaller value would reject most of them.
why.wait_hold_s: INITIAL. How long a WAIT must be read before the robot holds position: same as gesture_hold_s.
why.wait_timeout_s: DECIDED 2026-10-24 (Anisha): 20 s. After it the ask counts as unclear: ask again (from a new viewpoint, reask_shift_m), then abort, as in v3.
why.use_hand_crosscheck_as_tiebreak: false until the development evaluation has measured the MediaPipe world-landmark cross-check: when the roadmap leaves two branches, the finger direction would decide. Off = the ask is unclear (ask again).
why.two_view_enabled: DECIDED 2026-10-24 (Anisha). When the two depth readings of a POINT fit two different branches, the robot does not abort: it moves sideways by reask_shift_m (v3 value 0.4 m, to its right as it faces the person), reads again, and accepts the candidate that is consistent across both views. At most once per junction; the second view does not use up an ask. Still unclear -> ask again, then abort as before.
why.view_consistency_deg: INITIAL. Two readings of the same pointed direction (world yaw) from the two viewpoints agree within this many degrees. A 0.4 m shift at 2.0 m turns the camera by about 11 deg, which moves the mirror candidate by about 23 deg while the true direction stays put; 10 deg therefore separates them only if the angle noise is under about 6 deg. A larger shift (reask_shift_m) would separate them with more noise (docs/gesture_reader_v4.md: two-view study); Anisha decides.
why.reapproach_commander: DECIDED 2026-10-24 (Anisha). When the commander turns out to be another person than the one the robot approached (linked by bearing to a 360-camera person), the robot approaches the commander to approach_distance_m and asks again, at most once per junction; this ask does not use up an ask.
why.reask_shift_m: INITIAL v4 value, decided 2026-10-24 by Anisha, to be confirmed on development data. Overrides the v3 value 0.4 m (hri_control.json, frozen, unchanged): how far the robot moves to its right, back onto the 2.0 m circle, before looking again (the second view of an ambiguous POINT and the re-ask). Simulator two-view study (docs/gesture_reader_v4.md, not a measurement): at 10 deg angle noise 0.4 m resolved 18 of 20 ambiguous FORWARD and LEFT asks (2 wrong), 0.8 m resolved 20 of 20. A 0.8 m shift turns the camera by about 22 deg, which moves the mirror candidate by about 45 deg while the true direction stays put. A declared v4 difference from v3 (AUDIT.md section 14.4).
why.return_speed_mps: DECIDED 2026-11-17 (Anisha, AUDIT.md 16.20.5): the speed of the return to the junction point (return_to_junction) only: 0.8 m/s, the cruise speed of hri_control.json (drive.cruise_speed_mps), instead of the approach speed 0.4 m/s that the return reused. Reason: AUDIT.md 16.20.3 counterfactual (A3 detection on 20/20 on the old slots instead of 14/20; closest approach to a person and safety stops unchanged); the return is the reverse of the drive to the worker, which the clearance layout keeps 1.0 m from every worker, and the person-in-path stop stays active. Absent = the approach speed (the behaviour before). Must be above 0 and at most the cruise speed. v4 only.

stop_rule.why: DECIDED 2026-11-17 (AUDIT.md 16.19.7; chosen after the replay of 16.19.6, disclosed there). While the robot is stopped (|v| below robot_stopped_speed_mps, the value Nusrat's README uses for driving, in these controller states; the wait mode is the read state) the controller uses each person's reading_stopped (the reader's STOP rule with the 0.3 s stillness window, gesture_reader.json hand.stop_still_when_robot_stopped); while the robot moves it uses the reader's own reading, exactly as before. Absent or false = always the reader's own reading.

why.declared: DECIDED 2026-11-17 (AUDIT.md 16.19.2 items A, D, E), a v4 change declared before any final data. The v3 person-in-path stop itself is unchanged; this only acts after it has held for blocked_s. Unity testing waits for Nusrat's NavMesh rack fix.
why.blocked_s: Seconds stopped by the person-in-path stop behind the same person before the recovery starts: a person crossing the 1.2 m corridor clears it in about 1 s, so 15 s is a person who stands there; below the 20 s WAIT timeout; the step-5 deadlocks lasted 420 s.
why.person_moved_max_m: The blocking person's position moved less than this while the robot waited: a standing worker sways, a walking one does not stay within 0.3 m.
why.back_m: Straight back this far: from the 0.85 m standstill distance it leaves the person about 1.9 m away, the 2.0 m ask standoff the robot already holds safely.
why.back_speed_mps: Below the junction speed 0.35 m/s (braking distance 0.04 m). Nusrat measured reverse in Unity: v -0.2 m/s backed up 1.04 m, no drift.
why.side_m: The waypoint abeam of the person is this far to the clear side: corridor half width 0.6 m + robot half width 0.3 m + side margin 0.1 m. Checked on the ground-truth grid by Nusrat (free on every road, 1220 of 1220); the controller never reads that grid: the right side unless somebody is within this distance of the waypoints, else the left, else it keeps waiting.
why.beyond_m: The two waypoints are this far BEFORE and AFTER the person along the road, each side_m to the side: the leg between them runs parallel to the road at side_m from the person, then the normal path to the target.
why.max_attempts: Recoveries per blocking person; then the robot waits as v3 does (the run ends by the timeout).

why.enabled: Switch for the zoom on / off comparison runs (research question 3). Off: vertical_fov_deg is -1 (keep the default) on every command.
why.fov_default_deg: Unity default (CLAUDE.md verified facts: vertical FOV 60 deg).
why.fov_min_deg: INITIAL. Narrowest field of view. At 15 deg a hand (0.19 m) at 5 m fills about 14 per cent of the image height; narrower would lose the arm for any reading of POINT.
why.fov_max_deg: The widest (the default); the zoom only narrows and widens back to this.
why.hand_share: INITIAL. The hand box should fill this share of the image height. A hand is about 0.19 m: at 2 m (the ask distance) it fills 9 per cent of a 60 deg view; 0.25 would need about 22 deg. The arm-fit rule below keeps the shoulder and wrist in view, so at 2 m it is the arm, not the hand, that limits the zoom.
why.arm_fit_margin: INITIAL. The shoulder, elbow and wrist keypoints must stay inside the image with this margin on every side (POINT is read from them), so the zoom never narrows past the arm. Also the margin inside which the hand must stay centred, else it counts as lost.
why.hand_lost_s: INITIAL. Without a hand box for this long the view widens: 5 frames at 10 Hz.
why.widen_step_deg: INITIAL. When the hand has been lost for hand_lost_s the view widens by this much, and again by this much every hand_lost_s while it stays lost, up to fov_max_deg (10 deg every 0.5 s = 20 deg/s, inside max_change_deg_per_s).
why.max_change_deg_per_s: INITIAL. Largest change of the commanded field of view per second, so the picture does not jump.
why.tilt_enabled: P6, declared 2026-11-12 (Avatar/Config/upgrade_design.md section 5; supersedes AUDIT.md 14.15 decision (c), disclosed in section 15): while a commander is read the pan-tilt camera tilts up so the fit box (nose, shoulders, hips and the active arm's elbow and wrist) is centred vertically; the field of view then narrows until the hand fills hand_share, never narrower than the fit box with arm_fit_margin. With enabled false both the field of view and the tilt stay at their defaults (-1).
why.tilt_min_deg: Level (0). Up only: no hand is below the level camera at the asking distance, so -1 (the default, level) is never a real request.
why.tilt_max_deg: The 23 deg of a raised hand at 2 m (AUDIT.md 14.15) plus margin. Unity clamps to the same range (robot_unity_v4.json pan_tilt_camera.tilt_min_deg / tilt_max_deg; an Edit Mode test checks they are equal).
why.tilt_max_change_deg_per_s: Same rate as the field of view, so the picture does not jump.

why.declared: 2026-11-13 (AUDIT.md section 16, experiments A and B, faculty plan). Three ways to find out that a worker pointed a wrong direction, each from evidence the robot has, none from goal B. All three are false = the behaviour of every earlier commit, unchanged. Not tuned: no number here was set on results.
why.second_opinion: At a node with at least two people (360 camera, track ids) ask a second person after the first accepted answer; if they disagree ask a third and follow the majority; two people who disagree with nobody else present: ask the first person again, the majority of the three answers decides (the first counts twice); no strict majority among three = unclear (abort, fail safe). Answers rejected by reject_impossible are not votes. A person whose own asks are all rejected counts as no opinion and the next person is asked.
why.reject_impossible: Reject a resolved answer that cannot be a way on, with a logged reason: arrival (straight back along the road the robot came from), no_branch (no branch of the node within dialog.branch_match_max_deg of the pointed direction, or PROCEED at a node without a FORWARD branch), dead_end (the branch leads to a node of kind dead_end in the map). A rejection held for dialog.gesture_hold_s ends the ask at once and asks again (it uses an ask). Off = the existing silent drop: the ask runs to its window. Since 2026-11-13 (AUDIT.md 16.11) the switch also makes a pointed direction ambiguous when its branch was found but the OTHER of the two mirror-image depth readings is the arrival road (a worker pointing back along the arrival road can be read as the branch his mirror image lands on); the existing second view then decides, and it does not use up an ask.
why.backtrack: When every answer at a junction was rejected and the asks are used up (the robot would abort), return to the last decision junction and take its other branch: the one untried branch directly, or, with two untried, ask again there with the failed branch excluded; at most once per junction, one level only. Needs reject_impossible (it is the rejections that are the evidence); the controller refuses the combination backtrack true / reject_impossible false.
why.second_opinion_radius_m: DECIDED 2026-11-17 (AUDIT.md 16.19 item 2): a second opinion is asked only of a person within this distance of the junction whose NEAREST node of the roadmap is this junction, so the robot never drives toward another junction to ask (step 5, A3: a second opinion asked 3.7 m away at J2). 6.5 m: the farthest a worker of a junction stands from it in the layouts is 6.3 m (beside: 6.0 m before and 2.0 m to the side), and the junctions are 12.5 m apart. null or absent = everybody (the earlier behaviour).
why.checkpoint: DROPPED 2026-11-20 (AUDIT.md 16.26.9, after the final check of 16.26.8.1): the checkpoint workers (variants T3 and T4 of AUDIT.md 16.23 to 16.25.2) are not used in the finals. checkpoint false and next_junction_back false: the robot ignores checkpoint workers, and Unity needs none. T3 was not adopted (16.23.1). T4 was adopted on 2026-11-18 (16.24.3) and dropped by the stopping rule: its in-sample gains did not survive the readability model, +0.0 pp in B3 on and B4 on on fresh simulator seeds 101 to 140 (16.26.8.1). The on files are T0 exactly: second opinion + reject impossible, backtrack off. The checkpoint code stays in the controller, off by default (the guard final_guard_v4.py refuses a control file with any checkpoint key on).
why.max_opinions: From the plan: ask a second, if they disagree a third, and follow the majority = at most three answers per junction visit (one more dialog is allowed for the tie rule's re-ask of the first person).

hud.note: commander_id in the HUD is the 360-camera track id of the commander (linked by bearing, configs/v4/commander.json link_bearing_tol_deg), -1 when it cannot be linked.
